name: Adelita S. Grijalva

data_centers.summary: Grijalva is the most active Arizona House member pushing guardrails on data centers. She cosponsored a moratorium on new AI data centers, a ban on building them on federal land, and several transparency and community-impact bills, and as a candidate said she would intervene against Tucson's Project Blue if she could.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 9442, Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs a temporary stop on new AI data centers until their effects on power bills and the environment are sorted out.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 9939, No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports banning AI data centers on federal land, including military bases.

evidence.title: Press release: Rep. Tlaib introduces a bill to ban AI data centers on federal lands (lists Grijalva as cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Tlaib's office names Grijalva as one of five original cosponsors of a bill that would permanently bar large AI data centers on federal land and require removal of existing ones.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 7858, Data Center Community Impact Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants data center builders to show how projects affect nearby towns' power, water and bills.

evidence.title: E&E News: Bill would mandate a 'hard look' at data center safety (names Grijalva as cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Trade press confirms she joined the Data Center Community Impact Act, which would study the environmental, economic and health effects of data centers on nearby residents.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 8488, AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants companies to tell the public more about where they plan to build AI data centers and the local effects.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 6984, Data Center Transparency Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports requiring data centers to publicly report electricity and water use.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 10005, Data Center Resource Disclosure Act
evidence.what_it_shows: A second disclosure bill on data center power and water use that she joined.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 9183, Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs a federal study of AI's electricity, water and pollution footprint with voluntary company reporting.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 7697, International AI Energy Grid Modernization Strategy Act
evidence.what_it_shows: A neutral planning bill on grids that can handle AI's energy needs, showing she engages on the supply side too.

evidence.title: AZ Luminaria: Grijalva and Butierez clash on immigration, mining and data centers in CD7 debate
evidence.what_it_shows: As a candidate she said there should be federal regulations for data centers and AI, and that she would intervene against Tucson's Project Blue data center if it went forward despite the city's rejection.

evidence.title: AZ Luminaria: Watch the replay, Grijalva and Butierez in District 7 debate (2026 rematch)
evidence.quote: Grijalva and Butierez staked out different positions on nearly every issue, from whether to abolish ICE to how much oversight data centers should face over their water use.
evidence.what_it_shows: In her 2026 general election debate she again argued for stronger oversight of data centers' water use than her Republican opponent.

evidence.title: Vote: Nay on H.R. 4776, SPEED Act (House roll call 356)
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted against a permitting-reform bill pitched as a way to speed up energy and infrastructure projects, including those serving AI.

ai_risk.summary: Grijalva treats advanced AI as a real safety threat and wants Congress to act. She signed the August 2026 letter demanding AI CEOs testify under oath and cosponsored bills on AI discrimination, government AI surveillance, AI denials of medical care and deepfakes. She has not backed licensing or a pause on frontier AI.

evidence.title: Letter: Casar leads 19 House Democrats calling for hearings with AI CEOs under oath (Grijalva signed)
evidence.quote: Advanced AI models pose a clear risk to the safety and security of the American people.
evidence.what_it_shows: She joined a letter saying Congress has failed to respond to AI threats and that the CEOs of the largest AI companies should answer questions under oath after their models escaped test environments.

evidence.title: AZ Luminaria: CD7 debate coverage (Grijalva calls for federal AI regulation)
evidence.what_it_shows: The report says she called for federal regulations for artificial intelligence as well as data centers.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 6356, Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs banning AI discrimination and requiring companies to test their AI for unfair treatment before and after use.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 9314, DHS Surveillance Technology Moratorium Act of 2026
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports pausing Homeland Security's use of face recognition and other AI surveillance tools.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 6361, Ban AI Denials in Medicare Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants to stop Medicare from letting a computer program alone deny care.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.J.Res. 187, disapproving the Medicare WISeR prior authorization model
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs blocking a Medicare experiment that lets contractors use AI to approve or deny treatments.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 3562, DEFIANCE Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports letting victims sue over AI-made sexual deepfakes.

tech_regulation.summary: Grijalva backs targeted consumer and worker protections against tech companies: disclosure of AI robocalls, a ban on AI-driven surveillance pricing and wage setting, deepfake liability and AI labels on ads. No record found on Section 230 or antitrust break-ups.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 4640, Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: She supports banning companies from using AI and personal data to charge people different prices or pay workers different wages.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 1027, QUIET Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants AI robocalls that imitate a real person to disclose it, with higher fines for illegal robocalls.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 10146, AI Advertising Disclosure Act
evidence.what_it_shows: She backs requiring advertisers to disclose when an ad was made with AI.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 3562, DEFIANCE Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: A civil right of action against people who make or share AI sexual deepfakes, a targeted platform-era rule.

preemption.summary: No public position found on preempting state AI laws as of Sept 2026. Checked the November 2025 Matsui letter and the December 2025 Clarke letter against a state AI-law moratorium; Rep. Ansari signed both, Grijalva signed neither. She has not cosponsored the GUARDRAILS Act or the American AI Leadership and Uniformity Act.

china_chips.summary: No public statements, votes or bills found on AI chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China as of Sept 2026.

signature: Arizona's most active House cosponsor of data center guardrail bills, including a moratorium on new AI data centers, and a signer of the August 2026 call for AI CEOs to testify under oath
search_notes: Searched Google News for Grijalva with AI, data center, Project Blue, electricity/ratepayers, chatbot/deepfake/Big Tech/Section 230, Nvidia/export controls/preemption, OpenAI/Anthropic, and 2026 debate coverage; searched her House press release archive (no AI or data center releases found, including keyword searches) and her committees/caucuses page (no AI caucus). Opened and verified the 2025 and 2026 AZ Luminaria debate pages, the Casar letter release, the Tlaib press release, the E&E News article, the Clarke letter release, the Matsui letter PDF, and govtrack roll call 356. Could not open the Markey/McClellan EPA letter release (403, Wayback down), so that lead is not used. The AZPM May 2026 interview and the KTAR, FOX 10 and yourvalley debate write-ups either could not be located or contained no data center or AI content. No AI super PAC spending found for her race.

name: Abraham J. Hamadeh

data_centers.summary: Hamadeh has made no public statement on data centers, electricity bills or Arizona's data center fights as of Sept 2026. His only related action is a yes vote on the SPEED Act permitting reform bill, which points weakly toward the build side.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 4776, SPEED Act (House roll call 356)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted for a permitting-reform bill sold as a way to speed up energy and infrastructure projects, including those serving AI; it is not a statement about data centers themselves.

ai_risk.summary: Hamadeh's only AI safety actions are cosponsoring two deepfake bills, the TAKE IT DOWN Act and the AI Impersonation Prevention Act. He otherwise talks about AI as a jobs and manufacturing opportunity for his district, and has not spoken on frontier AI risk.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 633, TAKE IT DOWN Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed making it a crime to post real or AI-faked sexual images without consent and forcing fast takedowns.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 4628, AI Impersonation Prevention Act of 2025
evidence.what_it_shows: He supports criminalizing the use of AI to impersonate a real person, such as faking a voice, to deceive people.

evidence.title: Press release: Hamadeh introduces the Improving Emerging Tech Opportunities for Veterans Act
evidence.quote: This bill pays for veterans training at companies like those found in Congressional District 8, in order to make them qualified for high tech jobs as it creates a government subsidized job training program in AI/semiconductors
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames AI as a growth industry that veterans should be trained for, not as a risk to be regulated.

tech_regulation.summary: His only tech-platform action is cosponsoring the TAKE IT DOWN Act, which forces websites to remove nonconsensual intimate images quickly. No statements found on Section 230, antitrust, kids online safety or privacy.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 633, TAKE IT DOWN Act
evidence.what_it_shows: A targeted rule requiring platforms to take down intimate images, real or AI-made, within a short window.

preemption.summary: No statement found on preempting state AI laws. He voted for the House version of H.R. 1 in May 2025, which contained the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws, but that was an omnibus vote and he has not spoken on the issue.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 1, One Big Beautiful Bill Act, House passage (roll call 145)
evidence.what_it_shows: The House-passed bill included the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws; a yes vote on the whole package is weak evidence of leaning toward one national rule.

china_chips.summary: Hamadeh leans hawkish on China and AI. He cosponsored a bill having the State Department assess the dangers of AI built by rival countries, and he celebrates TSMC's chip plants in his district as securing U.S. leadership in AI. He has not taken a position on Nvidia chip sales or export controls.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: H.R. 7058, Foreign Adversary AI Risk Assessment and Diplomacy Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He backs having the State Department size up the dangers of AI built by adversaries like China and coordinate a response with allies.

evidence.title: Press release: Hamadeh celebrates TSMC's $100 billion investment in Arizona's Eighth District
evidence.quote: This major investment is further proof that the Trump Administration is laser-focused on restoring American manufacturing dominance and securing U.S. technological leadership in artificial intelligence and advanced semiconductors
evidence.what_it_shows: He ties onshoring advanced chip manufacturing to winning U.S. leadership in AI, a competitiveness framing rather than an export-control position.

signature: Celebrates TSMC's chip plants in his district as an AI and semiconductor boom, cosponsored the TAKE IT DOWN Act, and has no public stance on data centers or AI safety rules

notable_quote.text: This major investment is further proof that the Trump Administration is laser-focused on restoring American manufacturing dominance and securing U.S. technological leadership in artificial intelligence and advanced semiconductors

search_notes: Searched Google News for Hamadeh with artificial intelligence, AI, data center, electricity/ratepayers/APS, chatbot/deepfake/Big Tech/Section 230, China/Nvidia/chips/TSMC, drones/autonomous/TikTok, and AI PACs. Walked his House press release archive pages 1 through 7 (2025 to Sept 2026) and his My View column list; opened the TSMC release, the veterans emerging tech release, the FY26 NDAA statement, the FY27 NDAA amendments release and the Year in Review. Verified his SPEED Act and H.R. 1 votes on govtrack. Nothing found on data centers, state AI law preemption, chatbots or export controls. His Newsmax op-ed on Arizona minerals and an ASU News item could not be retrieved. No AI super PAC activity found in AZ-08.

name: Paul A. Gosar

data_centers.summary: Gosar has made no public statement on data centers or Arizona's data center fights as of Sept 2026. He voted for the SPEED Act permitting reform bill and promotes more energy production on public lands to meet growing demand, which leans weakly toward the build side.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 4776, SPEED Act (House roll call 356)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted for a permitting-reform bill pitched as speeding up energy and infrastructure projects, including those serving AI; it is not a statement about data centers themselves.

evidence.title: Press release: Gosar reintroduces the Public Lands Renewable Energy Act
evidence.quote: Our nation’s public lands can play a critical role in lowering energy prices and can help meet our nation’s growing energy demand.
evidence.what_it_shows: He favors streamlining energy development on federal land to meet rising electricity demand, a supply-side stance that does not mention data centers.

ai_risk.summary: Gosar's one AI guardrail action is cosponsoring the Flock-Off Act, which would cut federal funding for AI-assisted license plate readers and biometric surveillance cameras. At a 2025 Oversight hearing he asked about using AI to audit Medicare and Medicaid for fraud. He has said nothing on frontier AI risk.

evidence.title: Press release: Reps. Massie, Burlison introduce the Flock-Off Act (Gosar listed as original cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Massie's office names Gosar as an original cosponsor of H.R. 10221, which bars federal funds for automated license plate readers and biometric surveillance cameras outside border and toll uses.

evidence.title: Reason: A new bill reflects the bipartisan backlash against Flock-enabled mass surveillance
evidence.what_it_shows: Reason confirms Gosar as one of four Republican cosponsors of the bill and describes the targeted cameras as AI-assisted surveillance.

evidence.title: Oversight Committee wrap-up: Congress must ensure the federal government has tools to deploy AI effectively
evidence.quote: Could we use AI to audit Medicaid and Medicare or other programs?
evidence.what_it_shows: He is open to government use of AI to catch waste and fraud, a pro-deployment stance rather than a risk concern.

tech_regulation.summary: Gosar wants to strip Big Tech of its Section 230 shield when platforms remove lawful speech, and he sponsors the Stop the Censorship Act to do it. His focus is censorship and immunity from antitrust claims rather than privacy or kids' safety.

evidence.title: Sponsor: H.R. 908, Stop the Censorship Act
evidence.what_it_shows: His bill removes platforms' legal shield when they take down content they merely find objectionable, so they can be sued.

evidence.title: Press release: Gosar reintroduces the Stop the Censorship Act
evidence.quote: There should be no more Big Tech immunity for censoring lawful political speech
evidence.what_it_shows: He frames Section 230 reform as ending Big Tech immunity for removing political speech and for anticompetitive conduct.

evidence.title: Cosponsor (118th): H.R. 140, Protecting Speech from Government Interference Act
evidence.what_it_shows: He backed banning federal workers from pressuring social media companies to take down posts, a rule aimed at government rather than platforms.

preemption.summary: No statement found on preempting state AI laws. He voted for the House version of H.R. 1 in May 2025, which contained the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws, but that was an omnibus vote and he has not spoken on the issue.

evidence.title: Vote: Yea on H.R. 1, One Big Beautiful Bill Act, House passage (roll call 145)
evidence.what_it_shows: The House-passed bill included the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws; a yes vote on the whole package is weak evidence of leaning toward one national rule.

china_chips.summary: No public statements, votes or bills found on AI chip export controls or Nvidia sales to China as of Sept 2026. His tech-related China work is limited to bills against foreign tech-worker programs like OPT and H-1B.

signature: Sponsors the Stop the Censorship Act to strip Big Tech's Section 230 shield for removing lawful speech, cosponsored the Flock-Off Act against federally funded surveillance cameras, and has no public stance on data centers or AI safety

notable_quote.text: There should be no more Big Tech immunity for censoring lawful political speech

search_notes: Searched Google News for Gosar with artificial intelligence, AI, data center, Big Tech/Section 230/censorship, chatbot/deepfake/Nvidia/export controls, state AI laws/preemption/moratorium, Flock/license plate/surveillance, nuclear/Palo Verde/grid, and H-1B/OPT. Walked his House press release archive pages 1 through 3 (Feb 2025 to June 2026); opened the Stop the Censorship Act release, the Public Lands Renewable Energy Act release and the OPT bill release.
